output.title: Shipping Fee for Refrigerated Specialty Medication Packages
output.draft_text:
Q: How much is the shipping fee for a refrigerated specialty package?

A: Refrigerated (cold-chain) specialty medication packages are shipped [standard shipping method, e.g., overnight/priority] in temperature-controlled packaging. The shipping fee for a refrigerated specialty package is [fee amount or 'no charge'].

What to tell the member:
- Standard refrigerated shipping: [fee amount or 'no charge'].
- Expedited, Saturday, or special delivery requests: [fee amount, or 'not available'].
- Whether the fee depends on the member's plan or benefit: [yes/no; if yes, describe how].
- Whether the fee counts toward deductible or out-of-pocket maximum: [yes/no/not applicable].
- How the fee is billed: [e.g., added to copay at order time / billed separately / waived].

Exceptions and waivers: [conditions under which the fee is waived or changed, e.g., replacement of a damaged or temperature-compromised shipment, or 'none'].

If the member disputes a shipping charge or the situation is not covered above, [escalation path or team name, contact method].

Effective date of this fee information: [effective date].

author_checklist: Confirm the current shipping fee for standard refrigerated specialty packages, including whether there is no charge.
Confirm the standard shipping method used for refrigerated specialty packages.
Confirm whether expedited, Saturday, or other special delivery options exist and what they cost.
Confirm whether the fee varies by plan, benefit design, client, or line of business.
Confirm whether the shipping fee applies toward the deductible or out-of-pocket maximum.
Confirm how and when the fee is billed to the member.
Confirm any waiver conditions, such as replacement shipments for damaged or temperature-compromised packages.
Confirm the escalation path for shipping fee disputes or unusual situations.
Confirm the effective date and the source document or owner for this fee information.
Have pharmacy operations or the specialty pharmacy owner approve the content before publication.
